DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.12079.setting: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust; patients starting clozapine
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.12079.standard: Cardiac monitoring during clozapine initiation: baseline ECG and weekly troponin and CRP in the first 4 weeks (no standardised framework stated)

cycle1.result: Of 219 patients, 180 had complete data. Baseline ECG completed in 80%. No routine troponin monitoring identified; CRP testing infrequent.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.12079.other_findings: Tachycardia occurred in more than 40%; 15 referred to cardiology before initiation, 6 in the first 4 weeks and 5 thereafter; 12 (7%) discontinued clozapine early, mainly owing to tachycardia. Authors propose adding weekly troponin and CRP to mandatory blood tests.

DOI:10.1136/emermed-2019-rcem.42.setting: Scottish pre-hospital trauma teams and receiving hospitals with Code Red policy; national audit
DOI:10.1136/emermed-2019-rcem.42.standard: Recommendations of the Scottish Transfusion and Laboratory Support in Trauma (TLST) group from the previous Code Red audit

cycle1.result: Previous audit: median time from 999 call to Code Red activation 70 minutes; 70% received pre-hospital TXA; survival to discharge 63%.

DOI:10.1136/emermed-2019-rcem.42.intervention: Recommendations from the previous audit adopted to optimise transfusion support in major trauma

cycle2.result: 66 activations; 93% received blood components; pre-hospital transfusion in 48 patients (73%), a 300% increase; median time from 999 call to Code Red activation 37 minutes; 78% received pre-hospital TXA; CRC:FFP ratios improved; survival to discharge 66%.

DOI:10.1136/emermed-2019-rcem.42.other_findings: Survival improved despite increased ISS; further improvement needed in TXA administration and time to blood products.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10564.topic: Psychotropic prescribing in children with neurodevelopmental disorders
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10564.setting: Barnet Service for Children and Adolescents with Neurodevelopmental disorders (SCAN), Holly Oak Unit, Edgware Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10564.standard: NICE guidelines and the STOMP and STAMP pledges

cycle1.result: 19% of young people prescribed psychotropics (2020); 50% offered therapeutic interventions.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10564.intervention: Positive Behavioural Support (PBS) workshops introduced in SCAN

cycle2.result: 88/161 (55%) on psychiatric medication; clients offered therapeutic interventions rose from 50% to 91%; prescribing of psychotropics rose (19% in 2020 vs 24%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10564.other_findings: Of those on medication, 55% had ADHD, 77% ASD and 45% both; authors attribute the rise in prescribing to post-COVID case acuity.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.177.setting: Geriatric ambulatory care day hospital, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.177.standard: Weaning guidance for benzodiazepines and Z-drugs from the Canadian National Pain Centre

cycle1.result: 11/59 (19%) had a benzodiazepine or Z-drug on repeat prescription (benzodiazepine 5, Z-drug 5, both 1); none of those on benzodiazepines were being weaned.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.177.intervention: Notices placed in the consult room in the registrar's line of sight reminding them to consider weaning, with side effects and weaning guidance

cycle2.result: No change in benzodiazepine prescribing (5/59); non-significant increase in Z-drugs (9/59, p=0.26).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz103.177.other_findings: Of those on benzodiazepines, 4 of 6 had a documented psychiatric diagnosis and 1 of 6 was attending psychiatric services.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac126.065.setting: Healthcare for older people wards, Queens Medical Centre, Nottingham
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac126.065.standard: NICE: reassess anticoagulation for patients on warfarin with poor control (2 INR values <1.5 or >5, or 1 INR >8, in past 6 months; or TTR <65%)

cycle1.result: Warfarin correctly continued in 7/38 (18%); 26/32 (81%) with unstable INRs discharged on warfarin.

cycle2.result: Warfarin correctly continued in 9/28 (32%); 10/24 (42%) with unstable INRs discharged on warfarin (p = 0.0043, Fisher exact test).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac126.065.other_findings: Overall NICE compliance remained poor despite the trend to improvement; median age 87.5 vs 83 in the first audit.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.247.setting: Teledermatology service including GP referrals and a 2-week-wait cancer pathway, Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: 68% received a definitive outcome without clinic attendance, 27% referred to clinic; lesion-based referrals (n = 5781) 71% definitive; 2WW TD-only pathway (n = 2889) 79% definitive; inflammatory referrals 55% definitive, 42% clinic.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.247.other_findings: Progressive statistically significant improvements across audit cycles, attributed to medical photographers' image quality, consultant experience and direct-to-biopsy referrals.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad258.521.setting: Seven surgical wards, district general hospital
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad258.521.standard: Francis Inquiry Report (2013) Recommendation 236: all inpatients should have a nominated responsible clinician

cycle1.result: 71% did not know their surgeon's name and 62% did not know their nurse's name; 76% of ward whiteboards had correct nominated staff information; 2% of bed-headboards had the surgeon's details.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad258.521.intervention: Junior doctor education to encourage communication with patients about their responsible care team

cycle2.result: 14% improvement in awareness of surgeon's name; whiteboards correct 95%; bed-headboards with surgeon's details 24%.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.726.topic: Single instillation intravesical chemotherapy after TURBT
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.726.setting: 232 hospitals globally (RESECT study data); primary curative TURBT
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.726.standard: Guideline-recommended single instillation intravesical chemotherapy (SI-IVC) after TURBT for NMIBC

cycle1.result: SI-IVC given in 3075 (39%) cases (low grade 48%, high grade 32%). In low grade cases, reasons for non-administration: surgeon did not request it (68%), requested but not given (7%), never given at the hospital (25%).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.726.other_findings: Of 3566 not requested, 42% surgeon thought not indicated, 14.4% potential contraindications, 34% no reason; 837 (31%) of 2707 without documented contraindication had low grade disease and likely would have benefitted.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.021.topic: Calcium and vitamin D monitoring in sarcoidosis
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.021.setting: King's College Hospital sarcoidosis database with community primary care records
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.021.standard: Monitoring of serum calcium and vitamin D in sarcoidosis patients on calcium and/or vitamin D supplementation

cycle1.result: 46/102 (45%) had serum calcium and vitamin D measured in the community in the last 12 months.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.021.other_findings: One patient on vitamin D had hypercalcaemia; a CCG-wide prescribing alert was implemented afterwards.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.324.setting: Two acute psychiatric wards, Briary Wing, Harrogate District Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.324.standard: Local and national research and development standards for approaching inpatients about research

cycle1.result: Only one ward implemented local guidance; 13/14 noted as approached, but only 3 remembered a research leaflet and none were verbally informed; documentation present in 9 and nonspecific.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.324.other_findings: No process for re-approaching initially unwell patients or following up at discharge; an action plan with flow charts was proposed.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa620.setting: 51 UK rheumatology centres; British Society for Rheumatology multicentre SLE audit data
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa620.standard: BSR risk stratification guidance and scoring grid for shielding (used to classify, not audited against)

cycle1.result: 344 (34.3%) had a shielding score of 3 or more and would have been advised to shield.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa620.other_findings: Previous or current lupus nephritis 2.6 (1.9–3.4) times more likely to shield; Black 1.9 (1.3–2.8) and Asian 1.9 (1.3–2.7) times more likely than White people, persisting after controlling for nephritis.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae197.301.setting: Two UK centres; adults undergoing emergency laparotomy

cycle1.result: 1, 3 and 5-year survival 76%, 67% and 61%. NELA and ACS-NSQIP 30-day predicted mortality correlated with 1-year mortality (R²=1); at 3 years only NELA (R²=0.23, p<0.05); at 5 years NELA R²=0.61, p<0.001 and ACS-NSQIP R²=0.31, p<0.05.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae197.301.other_findings: Median age 70 years; NELA showed the stronger correlation.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad258.230.setting: Cardiothoracic surgery wards, large cardiothoracic surgery department
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad258.230.standard: Complete stocking of emergency chest drain boxes (target date June 2022)

cycle1.result: Missing equipment prevalent in emergency chest drain boxes (baseline number of missing items not stated).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad258.230.intervention: Revised stock checklist produced with the project champion, thoracic audit lead and procedural document team, introduced over two PDSA cycles

cycle2.result: 81% reduction in the 3-month average number of reported missing items; 92% increase in perceived confidence that the box will be correctly stocked.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad258.230.other_findings: A third PDSA cycle is introducing a single-use pre-packed chest drain insertion pack.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.258.topic: Chest physiotherapy after open liver surgery
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.258.setting: Open liver surgery patients, Hampshire Hospitals Foundation Trust, Basingstoke
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.258.standard: Early postoperative chest physiotherapy as part of the enhanced recovery protocol

cycle1.result: 18/50 (36%) received chest physiotherapy on POD1; 16 (32%) received none; PPCs 20%.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.258.intervention: Intensive preoperative patient education, poster campaign and increased engagement with physiotherapists about timely chest physiotherapy

cycle2.result: 20/36 (57%) received chest physiotherapy on POD1 (p=0.07); 7 (19%) received none (p=0.19); PPCs 8% (p=0.13).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae271.258.other_findings: Wards with higher physiotherapist:patient ratios delivered more POD1 physiotherapy (C1 63% vs 20%, p=0.001; C2 93% vs 30%, p=0.0001); median stay unchanged at 4 days.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.077.setting: Major Trauma Centre, University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.077.standard: No national guideline on routine post-operative pelvic radiographs after hemiarthroplasty

cycle1.result: Post-operative pelvic radiographs performed in 98% at mean 2.71 days; only 8.2% had a documented clinical indication; positive findings in 3.1% (one dislocation, two leg-length discrepancies).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.077.other_findings: 90.8% mobilised before imaging; 32% of documentation lacked reviewer attribution. An electronic proforma for targeted imaging is recommended.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.244.standard: Completion of the VTE prophylaxis admission assessment

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 35%; VTE risk assessment completed 50%; 'active VTE on admission' 30%; 'active VTE at 72 hours' 20%; 'risk assessment for VTE' form 40%.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 50%; VTE risk assessment 60%; 'active VTE on admission' 40%; 'active VTE at 72 hours' 40%; 'risk assessment for VTE' form 60%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.244.other_findings: Further work with junior doctors planned to improve completion.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab219.250.topic: Indeterminate FDG-PET brain reports in memory clinic
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab219.250.setting: Memory clinic, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust

cycle1.result: Of 134 scans, 22 definitively indeterminate; all had further outpatient follow-up; 20 developed dementia (11/20 parietal z scores >2) and 2 had mild cognitive impairment.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab219.250.other_findings: Authors recommend follow-up of indeterminate scans, particularly with parietal z scores above 2.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.276.topic: HbA1c monitoring in vascular surgery inpatients
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.276.setting: Vascular surgery department, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary (tertiary centre)

cycle1.result: Appropriate HbA1c re-checks on indicated admissions 25%; repeat HbA1c required in 38%; mean staff knowledge score 56%.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.276.intervention: Educational teaching programme on diabetes management for clinical staff

cycle2.result: Appropriate HbA1c re-checks on indicated admissions 86%; repeat HbA1c required in 50%; mean knowledge score 77%.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.276.other_findings: Mean pre-admission HbA1c was high (78.6 and 73.6 mmol/mol); referral for multidisciplinary diabetes optimisation is a further focus.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.136.topic: VTE prophylaxis prescribing in older inpatients
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.136.setting: Medicine for the elderly service, Connolly Hospital, Dublin (level 3 hospital)
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.136.standard: Prophylactic anticoagulation for all hospitalised older adults unless contraindicated; target 95%

cycle1.result: 80% of older adults admitted were receiving prophylactic anticoagulation.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.136.intervention: Cause and effect analysis then small tests of change over 4 PDSA cycles addressing history taking, clinician education, documentation, handover, medication reconciliation and pharmacy support

cycle2.result: 98.1% (104/106) receiving prophylactic anticoagulation; 83% after one month.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.136.other_findings: Only 2 patients lacked documentation of a reason for not prescribing.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac322.099.setting: Two general medical wards, Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth

cycle1.result: 25/55 patients at risk; documented next of kin discussion in 74%; treatment plan discussions 81%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac322.099.intervention: Education of the medical team and a written prompt in the patient's notes

cycle2.result: 39/71 patients at risk; documented next of kin discussion 82%; treatment plan discussions 97%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac322.099.other_findings: Discussions on escalation, DoLS, capacity and Mental Health Act slightly decreased; consent for data sharing rarely documented.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.238.setting: General adult psychiatry inpatient ward, Heddfan Adult Mental Health Unit, BCUHB, north Wales
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.238.standard: Questionnaire based on Royal College of Psychiatrists core training learning outcomes and textbooks; target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: GMC number recorded 30%; route of admission 4%; consultant name 8%; no personal history or formulation; nursing observation level 20%; many other items missing.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.238.other_findings: A clerking and physical health proforma is planned before re-audit.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.118.setting: Mental Health Service for Older Persons, Dublin North City Central (community)
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.118.standard: Irish Medication Safety Network (IMSN) guidance for prescribing and monitoring lithium therapy

cycle1.result: Poor compliance with lithium monitoring against the standard (figures not stated).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.118.intervention: Lithium monitoring pack inserted into patient files to prompt standardised monitoring

cycle2.result: Improvement in recording of blood monitoring (figures not stated).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.118.other_findings: A formal lithium clinic was recommended; the pack will be added to NCHD induction and MDT teaching.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.112.setting: Gerontological inpatient rehabilitation ward, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.112.standard: STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate medications

cycle1.result: 38 potentially inappropriate medications identified (10% of all prescriptions); 12 deprescribing opportunities taken, one a dose reduction.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.112.other_findings: Commonest PIMs were full-dose PPI (n=12), hypnotics (n=7) and inappropriate opioids (n=4) in high-risk groups; mean 11 medications per patient.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.040.setting: General surgery and ageing and complex medicine teams, Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh NHS Teaching Trust
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.040.standard: NELA best practice tariff KPI: geriatrician input for all patients over 80 and those over 65 with frailty

cycle1.result: 0 NELA referrals to ageing and complex medicine; 8% received geriatrician-led CGA in 2019–2020 (national average 27%).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.040.intervention: Standardised referral proforma and pathway, then a dedicated NELA nurse and an electronic referral order in a digital acute abdomen pathway with mandatory frailty scoring (three cycles)

cycle2.result: 18 NELA referrals received and completed (6 in March–June 2024 after the proforma); geriatrician review rose from 40% in March 2024 to 100% for November 2024 to January 2025 in NELA audit figures.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.040.other_findings: Geriatricians on the frailty session completed CGAs for all referred patients.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae197.406.setting: Single tertiary centre in Romania; adults undergoing emergency laparotomy

cycle1.result: Actual 30-day mortality 31.4% vs NELA predicted 5.78% (1.84;21.48) and ACS-NSQIP 5.5% (1.2;24.2); correlation with actual mortality R²=0.33 and R²=0.41 (both p<0.0001).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae197.406.other_findings: Both calculators underpredicted 30-day mortality despite strong correlation with each other (R²=0.88).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag018.295.setting: Healthcare professionals reviewing images, Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Initial diagnostic accuracy 65%; higher among consultants and with CT (P < 0.01).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag018.295.intervention: Teaching on four key distinguishing imaging features

cycle2.result: Accuracy improved to 81%, with carotid body tumours better identified (P < 0.05).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag018.295.other_findings: MRI and non-consultant reviewers were associated with lower confidence.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.820.setting: Cardiff Health Access Practice, primary care for refugees and asylum seekers
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.820.standard: All Wales pharmacological PTSD prescribing algorithm (Cardiff and Vale Traumatic Stress Service, based on NICE and ISTSS guidelines)

cycle1.result: Only 10/130 initiated on a first-line medication; 117 started on a fourth-line medication; none on second- or third-line medications.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.820.other_findings: The algorithm had not yet been fully introduced; teaching on the algorithm followed the audit.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.210.setting: Surgical unit 1, Holy Family Hospital, Rawalpindi Medical University
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.210.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Documentation Checklist (23 elements)

cycle1.result: Five elements absent in all notes (estimated blood loss, antibiotic prophylaxis, time-in, complications, nature of surgery: 0%); operative diagnosis 30%, OT staff names 43%, anaesthetist details 73%, incision 70%, DVT prophylaxis 3/37 (8.1%).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.210.intervention: Revised RCS-based operation note template, real-time theatre reminders and staff feedback at morning meetings

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in 22/23 elements: complications 98%, time-in 89%, estimated blood loss 96%, antibiotic prophylaxis 83%, DVT prophylaxis 80%; OT staff names least compliant (71%).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znag063.210.other_findings: Surgeon name, findings, postoperative instructions, assistant, procedure name and time out were already >95%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.407.topic: Epilepsy aetiology investigation in learning disability
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.407.setting: Epilepsy Service, Bromley Community Learning Disability Team, Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.407.standard: NICE and ILAE: 100% of patients should have sufficient aetiological investigation (dysmorphism assessment, neuroimaging and genomics as appropriate)

cycle1.result: Aetiology structural 42%, genetic 13%, infectious 5%, unknown 41% (n=31); 58% (n=18) of unknown had outstanding investigations, 72% (n=13) with no apparent reason.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.407.other_findings: Genomics was the commonest outstanding investigation (70%); 40% (n=12) newly eligible for whole genome sequencing.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.050.topic: Modified Barthel Index as functional outcome measure
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.050.setting: Stroke rehabilitation unit, St Columcille's Hospital, Loughlinstown, Dublin

cycle1.result: MBI scores increased from 41 to 63/100, average increase 22% (up to 49%); predicted 'unlikely to return home' fell from 56% to 38%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.050.other_findings: No significant correlation between MBI and Shah's predicted outcomes.

DOI:10.1111/anae.16187.topic: Airway and respiratory complications during anaesthesia
DOI:10.1111/anae.16187.setting: 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) of the Royal College of Anaesthetists; national survey and case reports

cycle1.result: Among 24,721 surveyed cases, 421 airway and 264 respiratory complications; commonest airway complications laryngospasm 157 (37%), airway failure 125 (30%), aspiration 27 (6%); emergency front of neck airway 1 in 8370.

DOI:10.1111/anae.16187.other_findings: Of 881 cardiac arrest reports, airway and respiratory complications accounted for 113 (13%) arrests and 32 (9%) deaths, hypoxaemia the commonest cause; six unrecognised oesophageal intubations, three causing arrest, with capnography misinterpretation recurrent.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.8.079.setting: Major trauma centre, Lancashire Teaching Hospitals, Preston; patients aged 65 and over
DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.8.079.standard: NHFD key performance indicators: orthogeriatric review within 72 hours, surgery within 36 hours, post-operative weight bearing, confusion assessment, discharge home

cycle1.result: Orthogeriatric review within 72 hours 84%; surgery within 36 hours 32% (over 36 hours in 92% of peri-prosthetic fractures); 37% not advised to fully weight bear; confusion assessment 84%; 61% discharged to prior place of living.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.8.079.other_findings: Care for non-hip femoral fractures fell short of hip fracture standards, especially time to surgery in peri-prosthetic fractures.

cycle1.result: 90-day mortality 395/9475 (4%).

cycle2.result: 90-day mortality 362/10,589 (3%), OR 0.93 (0.80–1.09), p = 0.4; days alive and out of hospital 1.0 (0.4–1.6) days longer, p < 0.001.

DOI:10.1111/anae.15554.other_findings: Changes were indistinguishable from longer-term trends over 2004–2013 (57,577 patients); Māori had worse outcomes than non-Māori.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.30.setting: Range of wards caring for older patients, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.30.standard: NICE and AMRC guidance on discharge summary content

cycle1.result: 13% of discharge summaries scored 'good' across the four main components (follow-up actions, medicines, clinical summary, functional assessment).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.30.intervention: Monthly audit with a live-feedback system to ward teams from February 2018 (suspended April to September 2019 due to staffing, then restarted)

cycle2.result: 31% scored 'good' (40% in March 2019, falling to 20% in July 2019 while feedback was suspended).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.30.other_findings: Quality deteriorated when feedback stopped and recovered quickly when it restarted.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.198.topic: Bone health assessment in Parkinson's disease
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.198.setting: Weekly Parkinson's Disease Interdisciplinary Clinic, age-related day hospital, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 36% had known osteoporosis, of whom 33% were not on treatment; 27% had a previous fragility fracture, 33% of these not on treatment; 27% had a DXA scan.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.198.intervention: 'Bone health' section added to the clinic proforma

cycle2.result: Suboptimal bone health management warranting intervention identified in 50%; 25% started calcium/cholecalciferol; 8.3% restarted denosumab; 8.3% counselled on denosumab; 8.3% repeat DXA booked; 33% had a DXA.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.198.other_findings: 42% were unsure of their osteoporosis diagnosis in cycle 2; over 66% had a history of falls.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-001943.setting: Assisted conception unit, Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-001943.standard: Local project targets for total cycle time and data administration time

cycle1.result: Average total cycle time for administrative steps around 17 days; data administration time around 30 min per patient.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-001943.intervention: Real-time data entry into a single data system (IDEAS) as part of clinical jobs, over five PDSA cycles plus two sustainability cycles

cycle2.result: Total cycle time cut to 0 or 1 days and data administration time to around 18 min; all metrics reliably within targets.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-001943.other_findings: Paper and spreadsheets removed, and a 2-yearly storage tank audit replaced by a rolling audit.

EPMC:PPR:PPR1253536.setting: Irish Hip Fracture Database (national clinical audit); realist evaluation protocol

cycle1.result: not reported

EPMC:PPR:PPR1253536.other_findings: Protocol for a realist evaluation using literature review, qualitative interviews and an expert panel to develop programme theories on how a national audit generates impact; no results reported.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.025.topic: Perineural catheter analgesia in hip fracture
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.025.setting: Acute pain team, Cork University Hospital (tertiary hospital)
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.025.standard: ESRA recommendation of regional analgesia (femoral or PENG block) for hip fracture

cycle1.result: Early catheter removal (<72 hours) in 23 cases (59%), 15 removed by patients with delirium.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.025.other_findings: Pre-existing cognitive impairment in 18 (40%) and postoperative delirium in 21 (49%); 16 (90%) of the cognitively impaired developed delirium. Practice under review.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.293.topic: Secondary prevention prescribing in vascular patients
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.293.setting: Vascular surgery department, Aberdeen Royal Infirmary (tertiary centre)
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.293.standard: Guidance-based secondary prevention with antiplatelets and statins

cycle1.result: Antiplatelets started by discharge in 36% of those admitted without antiplatelet or anticoagulant; statins started in 20% of those without lipid-lowering therapy; 15% discharged on no secondary prevention.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.293.intervention: Education on guidance-based secondary prevention and modification of the daily handover proforma to monitor prescribing

cycle2.result: Antiplatelet initiation 55% and statin initiation 41% in eligible patients; 13% discharged on no secondary prevention.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.293.other_findings: On admission 70% (pre) and 49% (post) were already on antithrombotic plus statin therapy.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.11.010.topic: COVID-19 green pathways in elective surgery
DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.11.010.setting: 46 centres in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; UK-FALCON national audit of foot and ankle surgery

cycle1.result: No significant difference in perioperative COVID-19 infection between blue and green pathways in phase 1 (p = .109, .923, .577).

cycle2.result: Significant reduction in infection on the green pathway pre-lockdown (p < .001) and during lockdown (p < .001). Overall infection 1.07% (69/6,470) blue vs 0.21% (9/4,280) green.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.11.010.other_findings: No significant difference in COVID-19 related mortality between pathways; 10,846 patients in total.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.302.setting: Orthopaedic service and fracture liaison service, Letterkenny University Hospital, Co. Donegal
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.302.standard: Fifth Irish Hip Fracture Standard (bone health assessment) and British Geriatrics Society guidance on IV zoledronate after hip fracture

cycle1.result: 100% reviewed by the fracture liaison service; bone protection recommended for 46 (60%) via GP letter; only 7/46 (15.2%) had started treatment at follow-up.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.302.other_findings: An IV zoledronate clinic for patients after hip fracture is being established.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.189.setting: Four extended care units for residents over 65, Our Lady's Hospice and Care Services, Dublin
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.189.standard: Two HSE standards for documentation of indication and duration on antimicrobial prescriptions

cycle1.result: Of 136 antimicrobial prescriptions, 63.24% had indication, 66.18% duration and 55.88% both documented; 55/84 residents (65.5%) had at least one antimicrobial.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.189.other_findings: Oral/enteral prescriptions had highest adherence (88.90%) vs topical 49.5%; no prophylactic prescriptions (n = 32) had indication or duration recorded.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.248.setting: Emergency department and geriatric ward, large teaching hospital, Cork
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.248.standard: National dementia care standards and local hospital group KPIs, including 4AT delirium screening

cycle1.result: 85% compliance with the 4AT tool; 17/20 charts had complete 4AT scores.

cycle2.result: 4AT compliance fell to 40%; 11/20 charts had scores recorded, only 8 fully completed.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afae178.248.other_findings: Environmental audit showed poor dementia-friendly compliance (signage, clutter, bedroom colour contrast); all ward staff trained in the Sunflower life story tool.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.001.topic: Routine preoperative ECG before cataract surgery
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.001.setting: Low-risk ophthalmic surgery under sedation, Singapore General Hospital
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.001.standard: International guidelines advising against routine preoperative ECG in low-risk ophthalmic surgery

cycle1.result: Cancellations 3%; 275 cardiology referrals.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.001.intervention: Phased removal of routine preoperative ECGs: randomised pilot (1,000 patients), then all cataract surgery under sedation, then all low-risk ophthalmic surgery under sedation

cycle2.result: 67 cancellations (0.65%); cardiology referrals fell 57% (275 to 116, p<0.0001); estimated savings SGD 733,738.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.001.other_findings: Phase three (9,955 cases) achieved an 83% reduction in ECG use with no preventable perioperative events; phase one showed no difference in events (4.0% vs 3.2%, p=0.79).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.037.setting: International multicentre cohort from the Oesophagogastric Anastomosis Audit (OGAA)

cycle1.result: Pulmonary complications lower after totally MIE than open and hybrid (31% vs 38% vs 39%, p=0.002; adjusted OR vs open 0.57).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.037.other_findings: MIE had higher anastomotic leak (16% vs 11% vs 11%, p=0.026) but similar 90-day mortality (3% vs 4% vs 3%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.513.topic: GP referrals to perinatal mental health
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.513.setting: Perinatal Mental Health Service, four localities

cycle1.result: 66% used the referral proforma and 20% a letter; 25% did not state antenatal or postnatal status; medication stopped in 10%, and 64% of those proformas were incomplete.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.513.other_findings: Reason for referral was mostly unclear and some referrals were illegible; discussions with GP practices and a re-audit are planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11652.setting: Edisford and Hyndburn psychiatric inpatient wards, Royal Blackburn Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11652.standard: DVLA and GMC standards: advise patients when mental state or medication may affect driving, inform them of duty to notify the DVLA, and document this

cycle1.result: 19 (95%) on psychotropics that may impair driving; only 1 had documented driving advice at discharge; no documented DVLA contact by clinicians.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11652.other_findings: Ward education on DVLA and GMC standards and a re-audit after 1 month are recommended.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.005.topic: Osteoporosis assessment in inflammatory bowel disease
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.005.setting: Inflammatory bowel disease outpatient clinic, Midlands Regional Hospital Mullingar
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.005.standard: European Crohn's and Colitis Organisation (ECCO) recommendations on bone protection in IBD

cycle1.result: All had >3 months systemic steroids; FRAX assessment in 2 (2%); DEXA ordered in 22 (21%), 7 (7%) by the IBD clinic; bone protection in 21 (20%).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afad156.005.other_findings: 39 of 150 charts lacked essential data, so FRAX scores could not be calculated; an intervention tool is being designed before re-audit.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2025.3.048.topic: Paediatric forearm fracture manipulation in the emergency department
DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2025.3.048.setting: 51 hospitals across Great Britain; national trainee-led collaborative audit (CURFFED)
DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2025.3.048.standard: BOAST standards for the early management of the paediatric forearm fracture

cycle1.result: Overall compliance with BOAST standards 63%; of 577 eligible for ED manipulation, 424 (73%) managed in ED and 89 (21%) needed later theatre manipulation; IV sedation in 28% (n=120).

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2025.3.048.other_findings: Survey of 683 clinicians: barriers to ED manipulation were staff availability (65.7%) and physical space (50.4%); orthopaedic consultants more likely than registrars to favour theatre reduction (OR 1.9).

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz102.29.setting: Large tertiary referral hospital, St James's Hospital, Dublin; patients with dementia who died in hospital
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz102.29.standard: NICE guidance that people with dementia should have every opportunity to discuss future care wishes

cycle1.result: Only 14% had an advance care plan; 22% had resuscitation status recorded on admission; palliative care involved in 40%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afz102.29.other_findings: Resuscitation status was mostly documented about 15 days before death; 2 patients had no status documented and 3 received CPR.

DOI:10.1111/anae.13423.setting: 12 UK cardiac surgical centres; Association of Cardiothoracic Anaesthetists national audit

cycle1.result: 5895 (31%) had preoperative anaemia (centre range 23% to 45%); anaemia independently associated with transfusion (OR 2.75), mortality (OR 1.42) and longer stay.

DOI:10.1111/anae.13423.other_findings: Regional variation remained after adjustment (p < 0.001); each 10 g/l fall in haemoglobin raised odds of transfusion by 43% and mortality by 16%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10628.setting: Tier 4 specialist eating disorder inpatient unit
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10628.standard: Six standards from NICE guidelines: DEXA after 9–12 months of anorexia nervosa, repeat every two years, professional interpretation and patient education

cycle1.result: 30% of eligible patients scanned; 6% had results explained by professionals; patient education documented in 50%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10628.intervention: Structured recommendations: DEXA integrated into admission protocols, improved documentation and multidisciplinary interpretation and patient education

cycle2.result: 62.5% of eligible patients scanned; 80% had results interpreted and explained; education documented in 80%; scanning interval adherence 100%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10628.other_findings: No documentation of hormonal treatments or discussion of scan utility before use.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11263.setting: Liaison psychiatry service, acute hospital, West London NHS
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11263.standard: GMC and DVLA guidance: assess driving status, advise and document

cycle1.result: Driving status documented in 5%; no documented DVLA advice when indicated.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11263.intervention: Driving status and DVLA advice prompt added to the assessment template, verbal and email reminders, sharing case learning and visual prompts in the team office (PDSA cycles)

cycle2.result: Driving status documented in 50% by week three; DVLA advice provided in 13.6%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11263.other_findings: Gaps persisted in giving DVLA advice once driving status was confirmed.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae197.515.topic: Index admission cholecystectomy for gallstone pancreatitis
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae197.515.setting: Single surgical unit, University Hospital Hairmyres, NHS Lanarkshire
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae197.515.standard: AUGIS guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy during index admission or within two weeks for surgically fit patients with mild to moderate gallstone pancreatitis

cycle1.result: 19 (16.5%) had inpatient cholecystectomy, 42 (36.5%) outpatient cholecystectomy, 4 (3.5%) declined, 10 (8.7%) unfit; no documented reason in 40 (34.8%).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae197.515.other_findings: Median length of stay 5.8 days; median Charlson index 4.5 in those with no documented reason.

DOI:10.1111/anae.16157.setting: UK hospitals; 12-month registry phase of the 7th National Audit Project (NAP7) of the Royal College of Anaesthetists

cycle1.result: Initial rhythm non-shockable in 723 (82%); 665 (75%) survived the initial event and 384 (52%) survived to discharge; favourable functional outcome in 249 (88%) survivors.

DOI:10.1111/anae.16157.other_findings: Care rated good in 464 (53%) and poor in 18 (2%), with poor elements in a further 245 (28%); care before arrest most often poor (92, 11%).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.685.topic: Perioperative practice in deceased donor kidney transplantation
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.685.setting: 14 UK transplant centres; National Transplant Access to Theatre (NTACT) prospective audit

cycle1.result: Pre-operative antibiotics 98.4%; consultant surgeon led 91.7% (n=409), consultant anaesthetist 61.4%; central lines 67.7%, arterial lines 44.2%, advanced haemodynamic monitoring 27.6%; goal-directed fluid therapy 71.7%.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae163.685.other_findings: Post-operatively 76.9% went to a transplant ward, 9.4% ICU and 10.8% HDU; significant variation in practice.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.169.setting: Rapid Access Frailty Assessment Unit, Midland Regional Hospital Tullamore
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.169.standard: NICE guidelines on PPI prescribing indications

cycle1.result: 63 (52.5%) prescribed a PPI; only 15 (23.8%) had a documented indication in line with NICE.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.169.other_findings: Only one record mentioned PPI for iatrogenic gastritis despite gastro-erosive drugs; no records mentioned deprescribing.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae197.007.setting: Two UK centres; adults undergoing emergency laparotomy

cycle1.result: Actual 30-day mortality 9.74% vs NELA predicted 9.8% and ACS-NSQIP 6.59%; only NELA correlated strongly with actual mortality (R²=0.31, p<0.0001).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae197.007.other_findings: Under 70s: actual 5.78%, NELA 5.53%, ACS-NSQIP 3.41%; over 70s: actual 13.96%, NELA 14.02%, ACS-NSQIP 9.76%, with weak correlation.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10558.topic: Anticholinergic burden review in cognitive impairment
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10558.setting: East Hub Older Adult Community Mental Health Team, BSMHFT
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10558.standard: NICE guidelines on assessing and optimising anticholinergic burden

cycle1.result: 24% of patients with an ACB score greater than 3 had no documented assessment of anticholinergic burden or medication optimisation.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10558.other_findings: Findings disseminated Trust-wide and an ACB calculator (medichec.com) adopted before re-audit.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.440.setting: Older people's inpatient ward, Kingfisher Court, Hertfordshire
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.440.standard: Trust protocol for admission blood tests including fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c

cycle1.result: 23 (57.5%) had HbA1c or plasma glucose on admission; only 6 (15%) had plasma glucose, not specified as fasted; 17 (42.5%) had neither.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.440.other_findings: One patient with diet-controlled diabetes (HbA1c 55 mmol/mol) was started on metformin; clerking proforma and induction changes proposed.
